transcript.text: Our Samsung combi microwave keeps whirring for a few minutes after it's finished and beeped, even with the door open. Old one never did that. Is the fan stuck on?

Probably not stuck. What you're hearing is very likely the cooling fan doing its job. Combi microwaves have a grill and a fan oven built in, so they get much hotter inside than a basic microwave. Most are designed to keep the cooling fan running for a few minutes after the beep to pull heat away from the electronics, the door and the cabinet around it. Opening the door doesn't stop it, because it's cooling the inside of the casing, not just the food space. A simpler microwave without grill or oven functions often doesn't need this, which is probably why your old one never did it. It would be a fault if it doesn't settle down. A few quick observations will tell you: 1. Time it after a normal cook. If it stops by itself within roughly 5 to 10 minutes, that's normal run-on. If it keeps going for 20 minutes or more, or never stops until you unplug it, the temperature sensing or control may be holding the fan on.
2. Compare cooking modes. A longer run-on after grill, convection or combi cooking, and a short one (or none) after a quick microwave reheat, is exactly what normal cooling looks like. A long run-on even after 30 seconds of plain microwaving on a cold machine is more suspicious.
3. Listen to the sound. A steady, smooth whirr is fine. Grinding, rattling, scraping or a whirr that gets louder over the weeks points to a worn or rubbing fan.
4. Check the vents. Make sure the vents (usually on the back, sides or top) aren't blocked by the wall, cupboards or things stacked on top, and that it has the clearance the manual asks for. Poor airflow makes it run hotter, so the fan runs longer. If it stops on its own, sounds smooth and cooks normally, you can leave it alone. It's protecting the machine. If it runs on indefinitely, makes grinding noises, smells hot or cuts out mid-cook, that needs looking at. Because the fan and its sensors sit inside the casing, that would be a job for an engineer rather than something to open up yourself.

Thanks. It stops by itself after a few minutes, always under 5, and it's longest after using the grill or oven. After a short reheat it barely runs. The sound is just a smooth whirr, no grinding, and no burning smell. Does that sound normal then?

Yes, that sounds completely normal. 1. It stops by itself in under 5 minutes, so nothing is holding it on.
2. It runs longest after the grill or oven and barely at all after a short reheat. That's the fan responding to how much heat has built up, which is exactly how the cooling is meant to work.
3. It's a smooth whirr with no grinding and no burning smell, so there's no sign of a worn or rubbing fan. There's no need to do anything. It's protecting the electronics and the cabinet around it, and many combi models behave this way. Keep an eye out for any change over time. - It starts running for 20 minutes or more, or doesn't stop until you unplug it.
• It runs on for a long time even after a quick reheat from cold.
• You notice a hot or burning smell.
• It cuts out partway through a cook. If any of those happen, stop using it and get it looked at. The fan and sensors sit inside the casing, so that's not something to open up yourself.

candidates: Normal cooling-fan run-on after cooking (combi models cool the electronics and cavity after use) (high)
Temperature sensor or control fault keeping the cooling fan running too long (low)
Worn or rubbing cooling fan making the run-on more noticeable (low)
